featuresTraits:
Build Direction: Sneaky Thief Rogue
- Level 3 guest PC built around hiding, striking with Sneak Attack, using dirty tricks, and surviving bad decisions.
- U Turn is funny at the table, but mechanically useful: Stealth, Sleight of Hand, Cunning Action, and Fast Hands all matter.

Expertise
- Stealth and Sleight of Hand use double proficiency.

Sneak Attack (2d6)
- Once per turn, deal +2d6 damage when you hit with a finesse or ranged weapon if you have advantage, or if an ally is within 5 ft of the target and you do not have disadvantage.

Thieves' Cant
- Knows criminal signs, coded phrases, and smuggler shorthand.

[Quick] Cunning Action
- Bonus Action: Dash, Disengage, or Hide.

Thief: Fast Hands
- Bonus Action: make a Sleight of Hand check, use thieves' tools to disarm a trap or open a lock, or take the Use an Object action.
- Good uses: cut a rope, throw sand, slam a door, scatter caltrops, pick a pocket, flip a latch, or grab something small and immediately deny it.

Thief: Second-Story Work
- Climbing no longer costs extra movement.
- Running jumps increase by Dexterity modifier (+3 ft).

Signature Flavor: Avocado Work (optional homebrew, 1/short rest)
- When U Turn hits with the avocado knife and applies Sneak Attack, choose one effect:
- Pit Splitter: target speed reduced by 10 ft until the start of U Turn's next turn.
- Clean Cut: U Turn does not provoke opportunity attacks from that target this turn.
- Soft Spot: the next ally to hit that target before U Turn's next turn deals +1d4 damage.

Rules Notes
- The avocado knife is mechanically a dagger.
- If avoiding homebrew, ignore Avocado Work and run him as a standard Thief Rogue.

backstory:
U Turn is a rogue, smuggler, and professional bad influence from a far-off coastal land where the laws are strict, the ports are corrupt, and everyone insists they are just moving spices. He was banished after getting caught smuggling a forbidden narcotic paste called green hush inside crates of preserved avocados. His official sentence was exile. His version is: "Banishment is just travel with paperwork."

After being forced out, he drifted from port to road to border town, doing courier work, debt collection, and occasional inventory correction. He eventually ran into Duldrick and Kian on a bad stretch of road. Kian had been cornered by bandits, and Duldrick was already in the middle of saving him. U Turn, who had absolutely not been hiding nearby, saw an opportunity to rob the bandits while they were distracted. The plan lasted almost eight seconds. One shout, one thrown bottle, and one questionable knife later, U Turn had somehow become part of the rescue.

He now refers to the whole event as a three-way strategic intervention. He travels with Duldrick and Kian because he owes Duldrick for not letting the bandits kill him, thinks Kian is good luck in a bad way, and suspects the Belligerent Five are walking toward money, trouble, or both.
notes: Guest PC. Table voice: "I don't sneak. I arrive privately." "People see a dagger, they get nervous. People see an avocado knife, they get confused. Confused is better." "Duldrick was doing the heroic thing. Kian was doing the hostage thing. I was doing the financially responsible thing."
